name: chicken schnitzel
instructions:
From Jennifer Segal, Once Upon a Chef — the schnitzel-style breaded chicken. Pounded chicken cutlets in a classical three-step dredge (flour + egg + seasoned italian breadcrumbs), pan-fried through in deeper oil until crisp and cooked through. Served BARE with a lemon wedge on the side (no sauce). Split off from chicken-piccata — same chicken prep, but crust leads rather than sauce.

UNTESTED so far.

SERVES 4. Prep 15 min, cook 15 min.

=== CHICKEN PREP ===

- 1 1/2 lb BONELESS SKINLESS CHICKEN BREASTS (breast preferred over thigh — see notes)
- Slice each breast in half horizontally, pound to 1/4-inch thickness (both steps matter — see notes)

=== INGREDIENTS ===

CHICKEN COAT (three-step dredge):
- 3 tbsp all-purpose flour
- 3/4 tsp salt + 1/4 tsp black pepper (for the flour dredge)
- 2 eggs
- 1 cup PANKO breadcrumbs + 1/4 tsp salt + a pinch each of garlic powder / oregano / dried parsley (see notes — swapped from seasoned italian to panko)

FRY:
- ~1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil (deeper than piccata — see cook notes)

SERVE:
- 1 lemon, cut into wedges (classical schnitzel accompaniment; no pan sauce)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. THREE-STEP DREDGE:
   a. Combine flour, 3/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp pepper in a large sealable bag. Add pounded chicken; seal and shake to coat evenly.
   b. Beat the eggs in a large shallow bowl. In another shallow bowl, mix the breadcrumbs with the 1/4 tsp salt.
   c. Dip each floured cutlet in the egg (letting excess drip off), then coat evenly in the breadcrumbs.
2. PAN-FRY (DEEPER OIL, COOK THROUGH): heat ~1/2 cup olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat (deeper pool than piccata — enough to shallow-fry the breaded cutlets). When shimmering, add the breaded chicken.
3. Cook until first side is deeply golden and crisp, 3-4 min. Flip; cook the second side another 3-4 min until deeply golden and CHICKEN IS COOKED THROUGH. Thicker breaded crust + more oil = one-step cook, no oven-hold needed (unlike piccata).
4. Drain briefly on a paper towel or wire rack.
5. Serve immediately with a lemon wedge on the side. NO pan sauce — bare crispy cutlet + lemon is the classical presentation.
notes:
Source: Jennifer Segal, Once Upon a Chef — the breading technique from her chicken piccata recipe, framed here as schnitzel (no sauce, deeper fry, cooked through in the pan). UNTESTED so far — log the first attempt when it happens.

=== BREAST > THIGH; SLICE THIN + POUND ===

Chicken BREAST is preferred over thigh here. The lean, uniform breast takes to the flour-egg-breadcrumb dredge and the skillet fry cleanly; thigh's higher fat + connective tissue works against the fast-and-hot fry and against the crisp-crust target.

TWO-STEP PREP — SLICE THIN, THEN POUND: both steps matter.
1. SLICE each breast in half horizontally. Thinner cutlets + doubles the yield.
2. POUND the sliced halves to an even 1/4-inch thickness (sealed bag, meat mallet or rolling pin). Chicken breasts taper — slicing alone doesn't fix that. The pound step evens out the thickness so the pan-fry is uniform.

Make-or-break prep. Do both.

=== THREE-STEP BREADING — FLOUR → EGG → PANKO (WITH ADDED SEASONINGS) ===

Same three-step shape as classical schnitzel: flour → egg → breadcrumbs. WHOLE EGG (not yolk-only) — the goal here is a hearty crisp crust that holds up on its own, not the maximally-golden yolk-crust that chicken-tenders variant A optimizes for.

PANKO OVER SEASONED ITALIAN BREADCRUMBS: swapped from Segal's original (which called for seasoned italian breadcrumbs) to PANKO. Panko's larger, drier flakes give the maximally crunchy crust that schnitzel wants — deeper crunch than fine italian breadcrumbs. Add the seasonings yourself (garlic powder, oregano, dried parsley, maybe parmesan) since panko is plain.

CONTRAST WITH CHICKEN-TENDERS: tenders uses regular / fine breadcrumbs — softer crumb texture reads more classical-american-tender than panko's aggressive crunch. Schnitzel wants the crunch; tenders wants the crumb. Different crust registers on the same breading family.

=== DEEPER OIL, COOK THROUGH IN THE PAN (NO OVEN-HOLD) ===

Schnitzel-style: cooks THROUGH in the pan (no oven-hold), using MORE OIL to compensate for the thicker breaded crust and the need to fully cook the chicken in one step.

- Use ~1/2 cup olive oil in a 12-inch pan (a deeper pool than piccata's just-coat-the-pan approach).
- Cook 3-4 min per side.
- Second side is where the interior finishes — check that the chicken is cooked through before pulling.
- Drain briefly on paper towel or wire rack.

If you WANT the piccata pan sauce, you can make it separately in another pan and spoon over — but the classical schnitzel presentation is bare + lemon wedge + vegetable side.

=== SERVE BARE WITH A LEMON WEDGE + TARTAR SAUCE ON THE SIDE ===

No pan sauce. Two dipping/finishing options that work well:
- LEMON WEDGE — classical schnitzel accompaniment; squeeze the lemon over the cutlet at the table.
- TARTAR SAUCE (see tartar-sauce recipe) — the primary dipping-sauce pairing. Mayonnaise + dill pickles + lemon juice + dijon + capers + dill; sits cleanly against the breaded cutlet.
- KETCHUP — also welcome (both schnitzel and chicken-tenders like ketchup).

Both together at the table is fine — squeeze lemon on the cutlet, tartar for dipping bites. This is where schnitzel diverges most from chicken-piccata (which is defined by its lemon-butter-caper PAN sauce spooned over the plated chicken, not a side dip).

=== FREEZER FRIES PAIR WELL ===

Freezer fries pair naturally with schnitzel — bake alongside in the oven (Ballpark-style plating: crispy cutlet + fries + tartar sauce for dipping both). Chicken-schnitzel and chicken-tenders share the freezer-fries pairing, but differ on the DIP: schnitzel takes tartar sauce; tenders take honey / barbecue (see chicken-tenders).

=== MAKE-AHEAD / FREEZER-FRIENDLY (BREADED CHICKEN) ===

Breaded chicken (before frying) can be refrigerated 4 hours ahead or FROZEN up to 3 months. Freeze on a baking sheet until firm (~1 hour), then transfer to a resealable freezer bag or airtight container with parchment between cutlets. Defrost in the fridge before cooking.

=== NO SAUTÉED VEGETABLES IN THE PAN ===

Same rule as chicken-piccata: don't add sautéed vegetables to the frying oil. Vegetables go as SIDES — braised or steamed, plated NEXT TO the schnitzel (green beans, braised celery, roasted carrots, potato-based sides).

=== PAIRINGS ===

- Green beans / braised celery (see marcella-lemon-celery)
- Roasted carrots
- Parmesan smashed potatoes
- Polenta
- Cabbage / kraut (leaning austrian-schnitzel register)
- Simple green salad

=== HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM CHICKEN-PICCATA ===

Same chicken prep (breast > thigh, slice + pound), same skillet-format. Divergences:
- COAT: schnitzel is three-step breaded with PANKO (crunchy heavy crust); piccata is a light seasoned FLOUR DREDGE only (no egg, no breadcrumbs).
- COOK: schnitzel is longer pan-fry in DEEPER OIL, cook through in one step (no oven-hold); piccata is short pan-fry + oven-hold (residual heat finishes; sauce made in the pan after).
- SAUCE: schnitzel is served BARE with a lemon wedge + tartar sauce on the side (NO pan sauce); piccata has the signature lemon-butter-caper pan sauce spooned over the plated chicken.
- WHY NOT BREADED + SAUCE (HYBRID): Segal's original piccata recipe used three-step breading + sauce. Removed from chicken-piccata — the sauce over a breaded crust makes the coating go soggy immediately. If you want breading, come here (no sauce, keeps the crust intact); if you want the sauce, go to chicken-piccata (light flour dredge, sauce over top).
- REACH FOR SCHNITZEL when you want a bare crispy panko-crunchy cutlet with dipping sauces on the side. Reach for chicken-piccata when you want the lemon-butter-caper sauce leading over a light-crusted cutlet.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- chicken-piccata: split off from the same file. Same chicken prep, different coat + cook + sauce.
- chicken-tenders: baked breaded-strip format (variant A of tenders is the closest technical parallel to this breading). Cousin recipe; different structural axis.
- chicken-with-vinegar, french-chicken-soup, coq-au-vin: other chicken dishes; different formats.
original_chef: Jennifer Segal (Once Upon a Chef) — the breading technique from her chicken piccata recipe.
